items.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: They didn’t have a bass at that time, and later when they added the bass Joe Comfort, who was a fine bassist.

ctx.x: I understand you had a pretty strong family upbringing in Los Angeles here, and was it a musical household?

Well not really but I was close to the Woodman brothers, Britt Woodman and his family. They were all musical and they all were playing when they were young kids, playing quite well. The father actually had them studying and practicing every day after school, you know he was really pushing them. So when I met the Woodman brothers, they were all about 13 or 14, and they were like professional musicians, finished already, because their dad stressed that. So of course that inspired us, Charlie Mingus and a bunch of…
Do you recall hearing, was there a certain kind of music that inspired you to go in the direction of jazz that you might have heard early on?
